text: Good morning, Ashley and Todd. After a few days without strikes, the relative calm in the region

has been broken with this latest exchange. CENTCOM says U.S. and Saudi fighter aircraft struck multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours. The unwarranted attacks against U.S. forces were not successful. The U.S. also says on Tuesday, the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on U.S. forces in the Middle East. All of the missiles were intercepted. A U.S. official tells the Associated Press the two attacks were not connected. The strikes, though, come on the same day that President Trump met with

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky. Netanyahu insists he and President Trump are on the same page when it comes to the war. Because the president is so clear. I mean, he's so—we have a common commitment. We don't want to see

this fanatic regime in Tehran have nuclear weapons to threaten every American and to threaten the peace of the world and to threaten the existence of Israel. So we have a common goal. And it's going to be achieved, either through diplomatic means or other means. But we're both committed to that.

Zelenskyy, meantime, is touting Ukraine's ability to destroy Iranian and Russian drones as he also asks for Patriot Defense Missiles to intercept Russian attacks. We want to stop this war. We're asking, you know, the president Trump wants and the Europeans want. Putin doesn't want. We are asking to stop this war each day to minimum to negotiate ceasefire for some period of time and give possibility for diplomats to negotiate. But Putin doesn't want.
So this is the problem. That's why we need to respond, be tough, be strong.
Today, there are reports that Iran has ruled out Amman's proposal for regional joint management
of the Strait of Hormuz, undermining the latest attempts to resuscitate the memo of understanding.
